A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PST study of gender bias in DALLE-3. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison after matching renamed and relocated content.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation and fairness-intervention experiments, human annotation agreement, and BLIP classification results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports additional analyses of stereotype adherence and bias amplification.

M1.justification: PST retains the same pairing of oppositely stereotyped identities, image generation, human annotation, and stereotype-adherence scoring. The fairness-intervention prompt is also retained. Renaming STS to SS and expanding the framework description do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 40 occupations and organizational-power setting using 36 occupations and eight role descriptors, with single-person and paired generation. V2's larger stated prompt inventory does not establish additional task, domain, language, or population coverage actually evaluated.

E2.justification: The single-person comparison, untreated versus fairness-intervened generation, and BLIP versus human annotation comparisons are retained. Stable Diffusion remains a failed-generation investigation; no new comparator is evaluated.

E3.justification: V1 Section 4.3 selects one power-role pair per occupation and samples images three times; v2 Section 4.2 reports sampling a role pair during each of three independent runs. Both report 216 generations, so this establishes a revised protocol description, not verified rerunning. V2 also introduces image-level rates for both or either subject adhering to stereotypes in Figure 4.

E4.justification: V2 Section 4.6 and Figures 7–8 add frequency-based breakdowns of stereotype adherence and amplified, reduced, or unchanged bias by gender and power group. These extend v1's score-level comparisons. The mitigation analysis, illustrative cases, Stable Diffusion failures, and BLIP investigation remain.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose three samplings for the relevant experiments and retain identical per-run results in Appendix F. Neither introduces confidence intervals, significance tests, seeds, or a new uncertainty-estimation practice. V2's added average Kappa rows summarize the existing agreement measurements.

E6.justification: Matched appendix results and mitigation scores are unchanged, including overall paired scores of 47.38 and 18.98. V2 adds Figure 4's biased-image percentages, including PST(Any) values of 74.3% and 59.7%, gender shares in Figure 7, amplification frequencies in Figure 8, and average Kappa values in Table 1. These are additional reported summaries, not performance gains.

T1.justification: The binary stereotype indicator and overall averaging equation remain mathematically equivalent. V2 renames STS to SS and retains stratified scoring without reprinting v1's separate micro-score equation. No changed scoring rule, theorem, proof, or formal assumption is established.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly claims a contribution of 1,952 prompts and elevates the limitations of prompt-based mitigation into the introduction and conclusion. The central claims that PST exposes occupational and organizational-power biases missed by single-person evaluation remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explicit English-only limitation and frames the retained mitigation overshoot result as a broader warning about uncontrollable prompt-based mitigation. V1 already acknowledged overshoot and controllability concerns, so this is a limited extension of interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 adds explicit prompt-construction details, default-hyperparameter disclosure, Stable Diffusion and BLIP license information, and a conditional promise to release code and data upon acceptance. It does not establish actual release. The new prompt inventory is internally inconsistent: Section 3.2.2 states 944 total prompts but describes 800 plus 1,152.

R1.justification: Most related work and research positioning remain. V2 removes reference entries for the DALLE-3 system card, Imagen, and LAION-5b. The differently formatted Karlo reference identifies the same retained work.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the title, abstract, introduction, method exposition, and conclusion. It organizes PST into task formulation, prompts, and metrics, moves dataset construction into the method section, consolidates cross-setting discussion, and changes terminology throughout.

P2.justification: V2 adds a framework diagram and percentage, pie, and sunburst displays; removes several earlier score-gap and power scatterplots; and merges v1 Tables 2–4 into one comparison table. It also revises Figure 1 and relocates retained examples and appendix tables, substantially changing visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2's framework diagram, consolidated Table 2, and reorganized explanations improve accessibility. However, its new prompt totals conflict, and Figure 4's both/any percentages do not reconcile with the retained stereotype scores under the stated definitions. With the underlying results largely unchanged, these new reporting inconsistencies counterbalance the presentation gains, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
